paper: ai-and-society/The Impact of AI on Developer Productivity. Evidence from GitHub Copilot
reason: A controlled experiment on the economic effect of an AI coding tool on developer productivity and careers fits economic and social effects of AI better than the LLM-agent or evaluation folders.
summary: Copilot field experiment: developers with the AI pair programmer finished an HTTP server task in JavaScript 55.8% faster than the control group, with heterogeneous effects suggesting help for people entering software careers.

paper: data-centric-ml/augmentation-and-synthetic-data/Fake it till you make it. Learning transferable representations from synthetic ImageNet clones
reason: Synthetic training data generated by Stable Diffusion for image classification, outside LLM pretraining, fits synthetic training data better than the diffusion or vision folders.
summary: Stable Diffusion clones of ImageNet generated from class names alone, with minimal class-agnostic prompt engineering, close much of the gap to real-image training for classification and match real data for transfer.

paper: data-centric-ml/data-quality-and-shift/Do ImageNet Classifiers Generalize to ImageNet
reason: Tests whether classifiers overfit reused test sets by building new CIFAR-10 and ImageNet test sets, a validation-pitfalls question; vision folder covers architectures and tasks, and data-quality-and-shift covers distribution shift more broadly.
summary: New CIFAR-10 and ImageNet test sets built by following the original creation process show accuracy drops of 3-15% on CIFAR-10 and 11-14% on ImageNet, caused by harder images rather than test-set adaptivity.

paper: data-centric-ml/labels-and-annotation/The Perspectivist Paradigm Shift. Assumptions and Challenges of Capturing Human Labels
reason: The paper is a position piece on annotator disagreement and subjectivity in human data labeling, which fits the annotation and label-noise folder.
summary: Position paper arguing that annotator disagreement is a valuable signal rather than noise to minimize, examining the assumptions about its causes and the practical and normative challenges of perspectivist labeling, with recommendations for the data labeling pipeline.

paper: data-centric-ml/weak-supervision/Snorkel. Rapid Training Data Creation with Weak Supervision
reason: Snorkel is the canonical weak supervision system, using labeling functions and data programming to create training labels without hand labeling.
summary: Snorkel: users write labeling functions and data programming denoises them without ground truth, giving 2.8x faster model building and 45.5% better performance than seven hours of hand labeling, and coming within 3.60% of large hand-curated training sets.

paper: deep-learning/A continual learning survey. Defying forgetting in classification tasks
reason: No continual-learning folder exists; catastrophic forgetting in general neural networks (not LLM-specific) fits best under deep-learning/theory, with deep-learning as the general parent.
summary: Continual learning survey: a taxonomy of methods for task-incremental classification, a framework for setting the stability-plasticity trade-off, and a comparison of 11 methods and 4 baselines on Tiny Imagenet, iNaturalist and a sequence of recognition datasets.

paper: deep-learning/architectures/Going Deeper with Convolutions
reason: Inception/GoogLeNet is a core CNN architecture paper, which fits the scope of core architectures and building blocks (CNNs).
summary: Inception: a multi-scale CNN design that grows depth and width at constant compute budget, with the 22-layer GoogLeNet setting the state of the art for classification and detection at ILSVRC'14.

paper: deep-learning/efficiency-and-compression/Distilling Task-Specific Knowledge from BERT into Simple Neural Networks
reason: Knowledge distillation of BERT into a small BiLSTM for NLP tasks; distillation of neural networks in general fits this folder (llm/efficiency covers LLMs, while BERT-era models are not LLMs).
summary: Distilling BERT into a single-layer BiLSTM, and a siamese variant for sentence pairs, matches ELMo on paraphrasing, inference and sentiment tasks with roughly 100 times fewer parameters and 15 times less inference time.

paper: experimentation-and-metrics/ab-testing/Trustworthy online controlled experiments. five puzzling outcomes explained
reason: Covers pitfalls and trustworthy analysis of online controlled experiments at scale, matching the ab-testing scope (OEC and other metric topics are secondary).
summary: Five puzzling Bing and other online controlled experiment outcomes, root-caused over person-weeks to months, expose pitfalls in the OEC, click tracking, effect trends, experiment length and power, and carryover effects.

paper: experimentation-and-metrics/causal-inference/A Large Scale Benchmark for Individual Treatment Effect Prediction and Uplift Modeling
reason: Covers uplift modeling and individual treatment effect estimation from randomized trial data, which matches the causal inference, uplift and counterfactual estimation scope.
summary: Criteo Uplift benchmark: 13.9 million samples from randomized control trials, 210x larger than prior datasets, with uplift modeling metrics and synthetic response surfaces for comparing ITE and uplift baselines at high statistical significance.

paper: experimentation-and-metrics/metric-design/Deconfounding User Satisfaction Estimation from Response Rate Bias
reason: Industrial recommender case study on user satisfaction survey data, with IPW and multi-task learning to correct response bias, fits deployed-at-scale recommenders better than the causal-inference or metric-design folders.
summary: Inverse propensity weighting in a shared-bottom multi-task network (satisfaction plus response-rate tasks) corrects response rate bias in survey-trained satisfaction models, after finding a positive correlation between response rate and ratings in a large-scale survey dataset.

paper: experimentation-and-metrics/variance-reduction/Consistent Transformation of Ratio Metrics for Efficient Online Controlled Experiments
reason: The paper transforms ratio metrics into user-level metrics so that sensitivity improvement techniques such as regression adjustment can be applied in A/B tests, which is the variance-reduction topic.
summary: Ratio metrics are transformed into user-level average metrics that preserve directionality and significance level, so user-level sensitivity techniques apply, giving up to +34% sensitivity rate improvement on hundreds of real search-engine A/B tests when combined with regression adjustment.

paper: generative-models/gans-and-vaes/Perceptual Losses for Real-Time Style Transfer and Super-Resolution
reason: Image transformation (style transfer, super-resolution) with feed-forward CNNs is a vision task; generative-models/gans-and-vaes is less fitting since it is not a generative model family paper.
summary: Perceptual Losses: feed-forward networks trained on high-level features from a pretrained network match Gatys et al. style transfer quality at three orders of magnitude lower cost and improve single-image super-resolution over per-pixel losses.

paper: graphs/graph-embeddings/Fast and Accurate Network Embeddings via Very Sparse Random Projection
reason: FastRP is a random-projection node embedding method compared against DeepWalk and node2vec, matching the folder's scope that names FastRP.
summary: FastRP: very sparse random projection of a degree-normalized, transitive node similarity matrix gives network embeddings over 4,000 times faster than DeepWalk and node2vec with comparable or better downstream performance.

paper: graphs/graph-neural-networks/A Comprehensive Survey on Graph Neural Networks
reason: A survey of GNN architectures, which this folder's scope explicitly covers (GNN architectures and surveys).
summary: A GNN survey that proposes a taxonomy of four categories (recurrent GNNs, convolutional GNNs, graph autoencoders, spatial-temporal GNNs) and covers applications, open-source code, benchmark datasets, evaluation and future directions.

paper: interpretability/explainability/Grad-CAM. Visual Explanations from Deep Networks via Gradient-based Localization
reason: Grad-CAM is a gradient-based saliency method for visual explanations of CNN predictions, matching the feature attribution and saliency scope.
summary: Grad-CAM: gradients of a target concept flowing into the final convolutional layer yield a coarse class-discriminative localization map for CNNs without architectural changes or re-training, outperforming prior methods on ILSVRC-15 weakly-supervised localization and helping untrained users tell a stronger network from a weaker one.

paper: interpretability/mechanistic/Transcoders Find Interpretable LLM Feature Circuits
reason: Circuit analysis with transcoders as a sparse MLP approximation is core mechanistic interpretability, alongside SAEs and circuits.
summary: Transcoders: sparse wide MLP approximations of dense MLP layers enable weights-based circuit analysis that factorizes into input-dependent and input-invariant terms, matching SAEs on sparsity, faithfulness and interpretability at 120M, 410M and 1.4B parameters.

paper: llm/agents/Reflexion. Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
reason: Reflexion is a language-agent framework that learns from trial-and-error through verbal self-reflection stored in an episodic memory buffer, which fits LLM agents best.
summary: Reflexion: agents verbally reflect on task feedback and keep the reflections in an episodic memory buffer, improving later trials without weight updates and reaching 91% pass@1 on HumanEval versus GPT-4's 80%.

paper: llm/architecture/Byte Latent Transformer. Patches Scale Better Than Tokens
reason: Byte-level LLM architecture with dynamic entropy-based patching replacing tokenization, which falls under tokenization and byte-level models in architecture.
summary: BLT: a byte-level LLM that groups bytes into dynamically sized patches by next-byte entropy, matching tokenization-based models in a flop-controlled scaling study up to 8B parameters and 4T training bytes while improving inference efficiency and robustness.

paper: llm/architecture/efficient-attention-and-long-context/Efficient Attention. Attention with Linear Complexities
reason: Proposes a linear-complexity attention equivalent to dot-product attention; the closest folder is the efficient attention one, though the evaluation is on vision tasks (detection, segmentation, stereo depth).
summary: Efficient attention: a linear-complexity mechanism equivalent to dot-product attention with far lower memory and compute, improving MS-COCO 2017 detectors and instance segmenters and reaching state-of-the-art stereo depth estimation on Scene Flow.

paper: llm/architecture/recurrent-and-state-space/RWKV. Reinventing RNNs for the Transformer Era
reason: RWKV is a linear-attention RNN alternative to transformers, matching the scope's named examples.
summary: RWKV: a linear-attention model that trains in parallel like a transformer and runs as an RNN with constant memory and compute at inference, scaled to 14B parameters and on par with similarly sized Transformers.

paper: llm/context/Retrieval meets Long Context Large Language Models
reason: Compares retrieval augmentation against context-window extension and combines them, centrally a RAG-versus-long-context study.
summary: Retrieval vs long context: a 4K-window LLM with simple retrieval matches a 16K positional-interpolation finetune at far lower compute, and retrieval-augmented Llama2-70B-32k beats GPT-3.5-turbo-16k and Davinci003 on nine long-context tasks.

paper: llm/efficiency/LLM Pruning and Distillation in Practice. The Minitron Approach
reason: Structured pruning plus knowledge distillation to compress LLMs falls under making LLMs cheaper via pruning and distillation.
summary: Minitron: depth and width pruning plus distillation, with a teacher-correction fine-tuning step for restricted pretraining data, compresses Mistral NeMo 12B to 8B and Llama 3.1 8B to 4B with far fewer training tokens than training from scratch.

paper: llm/evaluation/benchmarks/Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Software Tasks
reason: Proposes a benchmark-based metric (50% time horizon) for measuring LLM capabilities on long software tasks using RE-Bench, HCAST and new tasks.
summary: Time horizon metric: the human task length that models complete at 50% success is about 110 minutes for o3 and has doubled roughly every seven months since 2019.

paper: llm/evaluation/methods/Holistic Evaluation of Language Models
reason: HELM is a broad benchmark suite and evaluation framework for LLM capabilities across scenarios and metrics, so it fits benchmarks best.
summary: HELM: a multi-metric benchmark scoring 30 language models on 42 scenarios across 7 metrics (accuracy, calibration, robustness, fairness, bias, toxicity, efficiency), raising dense coverage of core scenarios from 17.9% to 96.0% and yielding 25 findings.

paper: llm/foundation-models/NVIDIA Nemotron 3. Efficient and Open Intelligence
reason: A model family technical white paper (Nemotron 3), which fits the model families and technical reports scope.
summary: Nemotron 3 (Nano, Super, Ultra): open hybrid Mamba–Transformer mixture-of-experts models with up to 1M-token context, LatentMoE and NVFP4 training for the larger two, and multi-environment RL post-training with reasoning budget control.

paper: llm/personalization/benchmarks/LaMP. When Large Language Models Meet Personalization
reason: LaMP is a benchmark for personalized LLM outputs, which fits the personalization benchmarks folder.
summary: LaMP: a benchmark of seven personalized tasks (three classification, four generation) with per-user profiles, plus retrieval augmentation over user items (term matching, semantic, time-aware) that improves zero-shot and fine-tuned LMs.

paper: llm/personalization/methods/A Roadmap to Pluralistic Alignment
reason: The paper argues that standard alignment (RLHF-style) procedures limit pluralism and may reduce distributional pluralism, so it fits preference-based alignment best; llm/behaviour and llm/personalization/methods are weaker fits.
summary: A roadmap to pluralistic alignment defining Overton, steerably and distributionally pluralistic models plus three benchmark classes, and arguing that standard alignment procedures may reduce distributional pluralism.

paper: llm/personalization/user-modelling/RecToM. A Benchmark for Evaluating Machine Theory of Mind in LLM-based Conversational Recommender
reason: A benchmark for theory-of-mind inference of user mental states in recommendation dialogues, matching the scope of benchmarks for user understanding (theory of mind) under personalization.
summary: RecToM: a benchmark of recommendation dialogues testing LLM theory of mind through Cognitive Inference and Behavioral Prediction, where models recognize mental states only partly and struggle to track evolving intentions and align strategies.

paper: llm/post-training/Large Language Model Post-Training. A Unified View of Off-Policy and On-Policy Learning
reason: A survey spanning SFT, preference optimization, RL and distillation across post-training stages, so it fits the parent folder rather than any single subfolder.
summary: Survey framing LLM post-training as off-policy versus on-policy learning, read through support expansion, policy reshaping and behavioral consolidation roles that unify SFT, preference optimization, RL and distillation.

paper: llm/post-training/data/Nemotron-4 340B Technical Report
reason: A technical report on an LLM model family (base, instruct, reward), which fits model families and technical reports.
summary: Nemotron-4 340B: open base, instruct and reward models sized to fit a single DGX H100 with 8 GPUs in FP8, aligned with over 98% synthetic data and a released data generation pipeline.

paper: llm/post-training/fine-tuning/LoRA. Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
reason: LoRA is a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method, which the fine-tuning folder explicitly names in its scope.
summary: LoRA: freezes pre-trained weights and injects trainable low-rank decomposition matrices into each Transformer layer, cutting trainable parameters 10,000x and GPU memory 3x versus GPT-3 175B fine-tuned with Adam, with on-par or better quality and no added inference latency.

paper: llm/post-training/preference-learning/Unpacking DPO and PPO. Disentangling Best Practices for Learning from Preference Feedback
reason: Systematic comparison of DPO vs PPO, preference data, and reward models in learning from preference feedback falls under RLHF and preference optimization.
summary: Tulu 2.5: a controlled study of preference data, learning algorithm, reward model and policy prompts finds data quality matters most (up to 8% gain in instruction following and truthfulness), with PPO beating DPO by up to 2.5% in math and 1.2% in general domains.

paper: llm/post-training/rl-for-reasoning/Beyond the 80 20 Rule. High-Entropy Minority Tokens Drive Effective Reinforcement Learning for LLM
reason: Analyzes RLVR through token entropy and improves it by restricting policy gradients to high-entropy forking tokens, which fits the RLVR analyses folder.
summary: High-entropy minority tokens: restricting RLVR policy gradients to the 20% highest-entropy 'forking' tokens matches full-gradient training on Qwen3-8B and beats it on Qwen3-32B (+11.04 AIME'25, +7.71 AIME'24) and Qwen3-14B (+4.79 AIME'25, +5.21 AIME'24).

paper: llm/routing/Adaptive-RAG. Learning to Adapt Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models through Question
reason: Adaptive RAG framework that routes questions among no-retrieval, single-step and iterative retrieval strategies based on predicted query complexity.
summary: Adaptive-RAG: a smaller LM classifier predicts query complexity to route each question among no-retrieval, single-step and iterative retrieval-augmented LLMs, improving QA efficiency and accuracy over adaptive-retrieval baselines.

paper: llm/uncertainty-and-hallucination/DoLa. Decoding by Contrasting Layers Improves Factuality in Large Language Models
reason: DoLa is a decoding method that reduces hallucinations and improves factuality, so it fits the hallucination folder better than efficiency or decoding-speed folders.
summary: DoLa: contrasting logits from later versus earlier transformer layers at decoding time surfaces factual knowledge without retrieval or fine-tuning, improving LLaMA models on TruthfulQA by 12-17% absolute points.

paper: ml-foundations/classical-ml/An Introduction to Locally Linear Embedding
reason: LLE is a classic unsupervised nonlinear dimensionality reduction method, and classical-ml covers clustering and dimensionality reduction.
summary: Locally linear embedding: an unsupervised algorithm that maps high-dimensional data into a single global low-dimensional coordinate system by preserving local linear reconstruction weights, with an optimization free of local minima, illustrated on images of lips.

paper: ml-foundations/evaluation-and-model-selection/Random Search for Hyper-Parameter Optimization
reason: Hyper-parameter optimization is covered under optimizers, schedules, hyperparameter transfer and training diagnostics; no dedicated hyperparameter-tuning folder exists.
summary: Random Search: randomly chosen trials find neural network models as good or better than grid search in a small fraction of the computation time, because only a few hyper-parameters matter on each data set.

paper: ml-foundations/tabular/TabPFN. A Transformer That Solves Small Tabular Classification Problems in a Second
reason: TabPFN is a tabular foundation model, a transformer for small tabular classification compared against boosted trees and AutoML.
summary: TabPFN: a transformer trained once on synthetic datasets from a causal prior does in-context classification of small tabular data in one forward pass, beating boosted trees and matching AutoML with up to 230x speedup (5700x on GPU).

paper: ml-systems/distributed-training/Large Scale Distributed Deep Networks
reason: DistBelief with Downpour SGD and Sandblaster L-BFGS is a classic paper on data-parallel distributed training at cluster scale.
summary: DistBelief: asynchronous Downpour SGD and distributed Sandblaster L-BFGS train a network 30x larger than previously reported on thousands of machines, reaching state-of-the-art on ImageNet (16 million images, 21k categories).

paper: ml-systems/inference-and-serving/FlexGen. High-Throughput Generative Inference of Large Language Models with a Single GPU
reason: FlexGen is an LLM inference engine that offloads weights and KV cache across GPU, CPU and disk for high-throughput batched serving, which fits the serving-engines scope.
summary: FlexGen: a linear-programming search over GPU, CPU and disk tensor placement plus 4-bit weight and attention-cache compression runs OPT-175B on a single 16GB GPU at 1 token/s with an effective batch size of 144.

paper: ml-systems/production-ml/Model Cards for Model Reporting
reason: Model cards are a documentation framework for transparent reporting of model performance across demographic groups, which fits fairness and bias best among general ML folders.
summary: Model cards: short documents accompanying released models that report benchmarked performance across cultural, demographic and intersectional groups, intended use contexts and evaluation details, shown with cards for a smiling-face detector and a toxic-comment classifier.

paper: nlp/generation-metrics/MAUVE. Measuring the Gap Between Neural Text and Human Text using Divergence Frontiers
reason: MAUVE is an automatic metric for comparing generated text to human text, matching the scope of BLEU/BERTScore-style generation metrics.
summary: MAUVE: divergence frontiers computed in a quantized embedding space compare a model's text distribution to human text, tracking known properties of generated text, model size and human judgments.

paper: nlp/pretrained-language-models/Revisiting Few-sample BERT Fine-tuning
reason: Study of fine-tuning BERT encoders and its instability in few-sample settings, squarely in BERT-era fine-tuning.
summary: Few-sample BERT fine-tuning instability traces to biased-gradient optimization, unused upper layers and too few training iterations, and fixing these shrinks the gains of recently proposed stabilization methods.

paper: nlp/tasks-and-methods/Bad Characters. Imperceptible NLP Attacks
reason: Black-box adversarial attacks using imperceptible Unicode encoding perturbations against deployed NLP systems fit the jailbreaks/prompt injection/attacks folder, which is the closest text-attack fit.
summary: Imperceptible encoding perturbations (invisible characters, homoglyphs, reorderings, deletions) break NLP systems in a black-box setting: one injection significantly degrades models, three functionally break most, including Microsoft and Google commercial systems.

paper: recommender-systems/collaborative-filtering/BPR. Bayesian Personalized Ranking from Implicit Feedback
reason: BPR is a pairwise ranking optimization criterion for matrix factorization and adaptive kNN on implicit feedback, which fits the matrix factorization and neighbourhood models folder.
summary: BPR-Opt: a Bayesian maximum-posterior pairwise ranking criterion trained by SGD with bootstrap sampling, outperforming standard learning for matrix factorization and adaptive kNN on implicit feedback.

paper: recommender-systems/deep-and-sequential/DeepFM. A Factorization-Machine based Neural Network for CTR Prediction
reason: DeepFM is a deep recommender architecture for CTR prediction, combining factorization machines with a deep network; it is a deep recommender model, not an ads-systems or collaborative-filtering paper.
summary: DeepFM: a factorization machine and a deep network sharing one raw-feature input learn low- and high-order feature interactions end to end, with no feature engineering beyond raw features, unlike Wide & Deep.

paper: reinforcement-learning/world-models/Diffusion for World Modeling. Visual Details Matter in Atari
reason: A diffusion-based world model for training RL agents on Atari, which falls under model-based RL and world models.
summary: DIAMOND: an RL agent trained inside a diffusion world model that keeps visual details lost in discrete latents, reaching a mean human normalized score of 1.46 on Atari 100k, a best for agents trained entirely in a world model.

paper: representation-learning/embeddings/ArcFace. Additive Angular Margin Loss for Deep Face Recognition
reason: ArcFace is an angular-margin softmax loss for learning discriminative face embeddings (metric learning); no face-recognition folder exists, and vision folders cover ViT/detection/segmentation/tracking rather than this.
summary: ArcFace: an additive angular margin on the softmax loss with a clear geometric interpretation, plus sub-center ArcFace that isolates noisy faces to purify web data and inversion of the trained model to generate identity-preserved faces.

paper: research-practice/Can large language models provide useful feedback on research papers. A large-scale empirical
reason: Evaluates GPT-4 as a generator of peer-review feedback, comparing it with human reviewers and through a user study; no folder covers LLMs for scientific reviewing, and this is closest to evaluation methodology.
summary: GPT-4 feedback on full paper PDFs overlaps with human reviewers (30.85% for Nature journals, 39.23% for ICLR) about as much as two human reviewers overlap each other (28.58%, 35.25%), and 57.4% of 308 surveyed researchers found it helpful.

paper: robotics-and-embodied/Learning Fine-Grained Bimanual Manipulation with Low-Cost Hardware
reason: Imitation learning for real-world bimanual robot manipulation on low-cost hardware fits the robot learning folder, which has no subfolders.
summary: ACT: a transformer that generates chunks of actions, trained by imitation on a sub-$20k teleoperated bimanual rig (ALOHA), learns 6 fine manipulation tasks at 80-90% success from 10 minutes of demonstrations.

paper: search-and-ranking/ads/Practical Lessons from Predicting Clicks on Ads at Facebook
reason: Click-through rate prediction for Facebook ads is squarely computational advertising CTR prediction.
summary: Facebook's ad click predictor feeds gradient-boosted decision tree outputs into logistic regression, beating either alone by over 3%, with historical user and ad features mattering far more than data freshness, learning rate or sampling choices.

paper: search-and-ranking/click-models-and-unbiased-ltr/Unbiased Learning to Rank Meets Reality. Lessons from Baidu's Large-Scale Search Dataset
reason: The paper empirically evaluates unbiased learning to rank techniques learning from biased clicks on the Baidu-ULTR dataset.
summary: Baidu-ULTR reproduction: standard unbiased LTR robustly improves click prediction but not consistently ranking performance, which depends strongly on ranking loss and query-document features.

paper: search-and-ranking/evaluation/Information Retrieval System Evaluation. Effort, Sensitivity, and Reliability
reason: Covers IR evaluation: significance testing of retrieval system comparisons, metric reliability (P@10 vs MAP), and test collection design.
summary: Revisits significance testing for IR comparisons: the t-test proves more reliable than the sign or Wilcoxon test and than a large percentage difference, past work overestimated test error, and assessor effort is better spent on more topics judged in less detail.

paper: search-and-ranking/indexing-and-classical-ir/SIMD Compression and the Intersection of Sorted Integers
reason: Covers compression of sorted integer posting lists in inverted indexes and SIMD intersection for conjunctive queries, which falls under inverted indexes and compression.
summary: SIMD-based integer compression (S4-BP128-D4, as little as 0.7 CPU cycles per decoded 32-bit integer) plus vectorized posting-list intersection and SIMD Galloping can double the speed of a state-of-the-art approach for conjunctive queries on GOV2 and ClueWeb09.

paper: search-and-ranking/learning-to-rank/Accuracy at the Top
reason: Optimizes a convex surrogate loss for precision at the top of a scoring function's ranking, a learning-to-rank problem for search engines.
summary: Accuracy at the Top: a convex surrogate for classification accuracy on the top τ-quantile of scores, with margin-based guarantees and better precision at the top than competing algorithms in most bipartite experiments.

paper: search-and-ranking/neural-ranking/Pretrained Transformers for Text Ranking. BERT and Beyond
reason: A survey of transformer-based text ranking, mainly BERT rerankers in multi-stage pipelines, which neural-ranking covers; dense retrieval is the second half but rerankers come first.
summary: Survey of transformers for text ranking, covering multi-stage rerankers (relevance classification, evidence aggregation, document and query expansion) and dense retrieval, with long documents and the effectiveness-efficiency tradeoff as recurring themes.

paper: search-and-ranking/search-systems/Beyond Ranking. Optimizing Whole-Page Presentation
reason: The paper learns whole-page presentation of heterogeneous vertical results on a SERP, which matches the 'whole-page presentation' scope of search systems.
summary: Whole-page presentation: a framework that learns query- and content-aware placement and styling of heterogeneous SERP results from data, outperforming a leading federated search presentation algorithm without relying on the probability ranking principle.

paper: trustworthy-ml/ai-safety/AI Control. Improving Safety Despite Intentional Subversion
reason: Safety protocols robust to a deliberately subversive untrusted model is a general AI safety (control) problem, not a jailbreak or prompt-injection attack, so the general AI-safety folder fits better than llm/safety-and-privacy.
summary: AI Control: safety protocols such as trusted editing by GPT-3.5 and untrusted monitoring by GPT-4 are tested against deliberate subversion by an untrusted GPT-4 writing backdoored code, and they improve substantially on simple baselines.

paper: vision-and-multimodal/vision/Mask R-CNN
reason: Mask R-CNN is an object detection and instance segmentation architecture, which falls under vision architectures and tasks (detection, segmentation).
summary: Mask R-CNN: adding a parallel mask-prediction branch to Faster R-CNN gives instance segmentation at 5 fps and outperforms all single-model entries on COCO segmentation, detection and keypoint tracks, including the 2016 winners.
